name: TN-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent DesJarlais has a large financial advantage
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 2%
No polls or expert ratings; forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, DesJarlais's incumbency and roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge over Broderick, and markets pricing Democratic odds at about 2% all point to a comfortable Republican hold. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the race sits in Safe R territory.
model.watch: A late surge in Democratic fundraising or outside spending, or a scandal involving the incumbent, would be the main way this moves toward competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Scott DesJarlais seeks another term in a Middle Tennessee district that leans about eleven points Republican. He enters the general election with a large financial edge, having raised over half a million dollars and holding nearly half a million on hand, while Democratic nominee Victoria Broderick has raised under $60,000 with minimal cash remaining. Independent candidates trail far behind in resources.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so expectations rest on the district's partisan lean, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Democrats only about a two percent chance. The fundamentals point to a solid Republican win, with the main uncertainty being the absence of direct polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
